sources.entry: Lima - Lima launches Linux virtual machines with automatic file sharing and port forwarding. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/lima-vm/lima)

summary.one_liner: Lima is a tool that launches Linux virtual machines on macOS (and other hosts) with automatic file sharing and port forwarding, similar to WSL2.
summary.what_it_does: Lima starts Linux virtual machines with automatic file sharing and port forwarding. It was originally created to bring containerd and nerdctl to Mac users, but the README says it can run non-container workloads too. The README says it also supports other container engines such as Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes, and non-macOS hosts such as Linux and NetBSD. Basic usage is through the limactl command and a lima wrapper that runs Linux commands inside the VM. Predefined templates such as template:docker and template:k8s set up those engines. The README also describes SBOM outputs in CycloneDX format, with "app" and "mod" variants.
use_cases: run Linux commands on a Mac
run containers with containerd and nerdctl on macOS
run Docker containers on macOS without Docker Desktop
spin up a local Kubernetes cluster in a VM
share host files with a Linux VM
forward ports from a Linux VM to the host
notable: Automatic file sharing and port forwarding between host and Linux VM, similar to WSL2
Prebuilt templates for Docker and Kubernetes (template:docker, template:k8s)
Supports containerd/nerdctl as the original focus, plus Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes
Publishes CycloneDX SBOMs in 'app' and 'mod' variants
caveats: The README does not list system requirements or supported macOS versions.
The README gives no license name, so the license is unknown from the README.
The README links to external docs for further information, and several links in the README are empty.
